title: NEET PG — General Surgery | Wound Healing Sutures
description: Subject-wise test on Wound Healing Sutures (General Surgery) for NEET PG. 35Q.

questions.question: A 35-year-old male sustains a clean laceration to his forearm. Which phase of wound healing is primarily characterized by the formation of granulation tissue, neovascularization, and re-epithelialization?

options.explanation: The inflammatory phase involves initial immune response.
The maturation phase involves collagen remodeling.
The proliferative phase is characterized by the formation of granulation tissue, neovascularization, and re-epithelialization.
Hemostasis is the immediate response to stop bleeding.

questions.explanation: The proliferative phase (also known as the fibroblastic phase) is characterized by the formation of granulation tissue, which is rich in fibroblasts, new capillaries (neovascularization), and collagen deposition. Re-epithelialization also occurs during this phase as epithelial cells migrate across the wound surface.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes a key advantage of using a monofilament suture over a multifilament (braided) suture for skin closure?

options.text: Superior knot security, requiring fewer throws
options.explanation: Multifilament sutures generally have better knot security.
Tensile strength varies by material, not solely by monofilament/multifilament structure.

options.text: Reduced tissue drag and lower risk of bacterial colonization
options.explanation: Monofilament sutures have a smooth surface, reducing tissue drag and bacterial colonization.
Multifilament sutures generally have better handling.

questions.explanation: Monofilament sutures have a smooth surface, which results in less tissue drag as they pass through tissues. This smooth surface also makes them less prone to bacterial harborage and colonization compared to braided sutures, thus theoretically reducing the risk of surgical site infection.

questions.question: A surgeon is performing a primary repair of a perforated duodenal ulcer in an otherwise healthy 40-year-old patient. Which type of synthetic absorbable suture would be most appropriate for the seromuscular layer, considering the need for good initial tensile strength and a predictable absorption profile over 2-3 weeks?

options.explanation: PDS retains strength for much longer (up to 6 weeks), which might be excessive for a primary duodenal repair.
Polyglactin 910 (Vicryl) has a suitable absorption profile for gastrointestinal anastomoses.
Chromic catgut has a less predictable absorption and can provoke more tissue reaction.
Monocryl is faster absorbing and has less initial strength, making it less ideal for high-stress GI repairs.

questions.explanation: Polyglactin 910 (Vicryl) retains approximately 75% of its tensile strength at 2 weeks and 50% at 3 weeks, with complete absorption by 56-70 days.

questions.question: A 55-year-old patient undergoes an incisional hernia repair. The surgeon needs to close the fascial defect with a material that provides prolonged tensile strength and minimal tissue reaction for permanent support. Which suture material would be the most suitable choice for this purpose?

options.explanation: Plain catgut is absorbable and would not provide permanent support.
Polypropylene provides prolonged tensile strength and minimal tissue reaction for permanent support.
Polyglycolic acid is absorbable and would not provide permanent support.
Silk is non-absorbable but is a multifilament with higher tissue reactivity and can lose significant tensile strength over time.

questions.explanation: Polypropylene (e.g., Prolene) is a non-absorbable monofilament suture known for its high tensile strength, minimal tissue reactivity, and long-term retention of strength.

questions.question: A patient presents with a heavily contaminated traumatic wound to the leg, involving significant tissue loss and devitalized tissue. After thorough surgical debridement, the wound is left open, packed, and plans are made for delayed primary closure in 4-5 days if no signs of infection develop. This approach exemplifies which type of wound healing?

options.explanation: Primary intention involves immediate closure of clean wounds.
Secondary intention involves leaving a wound open to heal by granulation, contraction.
Tertiary intention involves delayed primary closure after debridement and observation for infection.
Epithelialization is a process of wound healing, not a type of wound healing.

questions.explanation: Tertiary intention (also known as delayed primary closure) involves leaving a contaminated or heavily colonized wound open for a period (typically 3-7 days) after debridement to allow for observation and prevention of infection.

questions.question: A 45-year-old male undergoes an appendectomy. On post-operative day 3, the wound shows mild erythema and induration around the incision edges, with minimal serous discharge. Which phase of wound healing is predominantly active at this stage?

options.explanation: The remodeling phase occurs much later in the wound healing process, after the proliferative phase.
The proliferative phase typically begins around day 3-5, but is not the predominant phase on post-operative day 3.
The inflammatory phase is the initial phase of wound healing, characterized by vascular changes, leukocyte infiltration, and the release of growth factors and cytokines.
The maturation phase occurs even later than the remodeling phase, and is characterized by the strengthening of the wound.

questions.explanation: Post-operative day 3 is typically dominated by the inflammatory phase of wound healing. This phase is characterized by vascular changes (erythema, swelling), leukocyte infiltration (neutrophils, macrophages) to clear debris and bacteria, and the release of growth factors and cytokines, preparing the wound for subsequent repair. The proliferative phase typically begins around day 3-5, while remodeling and maturation occur much later.

questions.question: A surgeon is preparing for a laparotomy. Which of the following suture materials is an example of a natural, absorbable, multifilament suture?

options.explanation: PDS is synthetic, monofilament, absorbable.
Vicryl is synthetic, multifilament, absorbable.
Surgical gut (catgut) is derived from purified collagen of sheep or bovine intestine (natural), is absorbed by enzymatic degradation (absorbable), and is twisted/braided (multifilament).
Prolene is synthetic, monofilament, non-absorbable.

questions.explanation: Surgical gut (catgut) is derived from purified collagen of sheep or bovine intestine (natural), is absorbed by enzymatic degradation (absorbable), and is twisted/braided (multifilament).

questions.question: A 35-year-old male presents with a traumatic laceration on the forearm after a road traffic accident. The wound is 5 cm long, 1 cm deep, and moderately contaminated with debris. Which of the following suture materials is MOST appropriate for primary closure of this wound?

Poliglecaprone 25 is an absorbable suture with excellent handling properties and moderate tissue reactivity, making it ideal for contaminated wounds

Polypropylene is non-absorbable and less ideal for contaminated tissue

questions.question: A 24-year-old female undergoes appendectomy. The surgeon uses interrupted sutures for abdominal wall closure. Which of the following is the PRIMARY advantage of interrupted sutures in this scenario?

Interrupted sutures do not necessarily promote better wound healing
Interrupted sutures distribute tension evenly and allow selective removal if infection occurs, reducing dehiscence risk
Interrupted sutures do not necessarily reduce tissue reactivity

questions.question: A patient develops a wound infection 5 days after inguinal hernia repair. The surgeon removes a few sutures, and purulent discharge is noted. Which type of suture material is MOST likely to have caused this complication?

Polydioxanone is an absorbable suture with low infection risk
Silk is a braided, non-absorbable suture that promotes bacterial colonization and is associated with higher infection rates
Nylon is a monofilament, non-absorbable suture with lower infection risk compared to braided sutures

questions.question: During a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, the surgeon uses a stapler to close the cystic duct. Which of the following BEST describes the type of wound healing expected at the stapled site?

options.explanation: Primary intention healing occurs in clean, uninfected wounds
Secondary intention healing occurs in wounds with significant tissue loss or infection
Stapled or sutured wounds in clean-contaminated surgeries like cholecystectomy heal by tertiary intention (delayed primary closure) due to the controlled contamination and absence of dead space
Delayed primary closure is a type of wound management, not a type of wound healing

questions.explanation: Stapled or sutured wounds in clean-contaminated surgeries like cholecystectomy heal by tertiary intention (delayed primary closure) due to the controlled contamination and absence of dead space.

questions.question: A 50-year-old diabetic male undergoes debridement of a diabetic foot ulcer. The wound is left open for secondary closure. Which of the following factors is MOST likely to impair wound healing in this patient?

Diabetes mellitus is a major systemic factor impairing wound healing due to microvascular damage, impaired leukocyte function, and delayed collagen synthesis
Obesity can impair wound healing, but it is not the most critical factor in this context
Smoking can impair wound healing, but it is not the most critical factor in this context

questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus is a major systemic factor impairing wound healing due to microvascular damage, impaired leukocyte function, and delayed collagen synthesis.

The vertical mattress suture does not primarily reduce wound tension

3-0 sutures are still too large for delicate skin areas like the palm
For facial or delicate skin areas like the palm, 4-0 or 5-0 sutures are ideal
5-0 sutures are also ideal, but 4-0 provides adequate strength without excessive tissue reaction

Interrupted sutures are less likely to cause keloid formation

Continuous sutures are less likely to cause keloid formation

Polyglycolic acid (e.g., Dexon) is a synthetic absorbable suture commonly used in contaminated wounds due to its predictable absorption and low tissue reactivity

questions.question: A 35-year-old male presents with a lacerated wound on his forearm that was sutured 7 days ago. On examination, the wound edges appear well-approximated but there is a serous discharge. Which of the following types of healing is most likely occurring in this wound?

options.explanation: Primary healing occurs when the wound is closed primarily and heals quickly without complications.
Secondary healing involves granulation tissue formation and wound contraction, which is likely occurring here due to the discharge.
Tertiary healing (delayed primary closure) would involve reopening the wound for debridement and closure later, which is not described.
Delayed primary healing is a type of healing where the wound is left open for a few days before being closed, which is not the case here.

questions.explanation: The wound shows signs of infection (serous discharge) despite primary closure, indicating that healing is not progressing as expected. Secondary healing involves granulation tissue formation and wound contraction, which is likely occurring here due to the discharge.

Polydioxanone (PDS) is a synthetic, absorbable suture with prolonged strength retention, making it ideal for fascial closure where prolonged support is needed.
Silk and nylon are non-absorbable and not typically used for peritoneal closure.

questions.explanation: Polydioxanone (PDS) is a synthetic, absorbable suture with prolonged strength retention, making it ideal for fascial closure where prolonged support is needed.

High platelet count does not impair healing.
Vitamin C aids collagen synthesis and wound healing.

Pseudomonas is more common in burn or chronic wounds.
Clostridium is more common in contaminated wounds with devitalized tissue.

Subcuticular sutures are not easily removable.
Subcuticular sutures do not specifically reduce dehiscence risk.

Stainless steel wire is rigid and not suitable for soft tissue.

questions.question: A surgeon is performing a vascular anastomosis using 6-0 polypropylene sutures. Which of the following is the primary purpose of using a fine suture in this scenario?

options.text: To minimize tissue trauma and reduce intimal damage

Chromic catgut is an absorbable suture material, but it may not be as suitable for skin closure as Monocryl.
Monocryl is a monofilament absorbable suture material that is suitable for skin closure, especially in areas where cosmetic outcome is important, such as the scalp.

questions.question: A 35-year-old patient undergoes an appendectomy and the surgeon decides to close the skin with staples. Which of the following is the primary advantage of using staples over sutures for skin closure?

options.explanation: Reduced risk of wound infection is not the primary advantage of using staples over sutures for skin closure.
Increased tensile strength is not the primary advantage of using staples over sutures for skin closure.
The primary advantage of using staples over sutures for skin closure is indeed the faster closure time.
Improved cosmetic outcome is not the primary advantage of using staples over sutures for skin closure.

questions.explanation: The primary advantage of using staples over sutures for skin closure is indeed the faster closure time, as staples can be applied more quickly than sutures, which is particularly beneficial in long or complex incisions.

questions.question: A patient presents with a wound that is not healing due to a lack of growth factors. Which of the following growth factors plays a crucial role in the proliferation phase of wound healing?

options.explanation: Platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) is not the primary growth factor that plays a crucial role in the proliferation phase of wound healing.
Transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) is not the primary growth factor that plays a crucial role in the proliferation phase of wound healing.
Epidermal growth factor (EGF) plays a crucial role in the proliferation phase of wound healing.
Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is not the primary growth factor that plays a crucial role in the proliferation phase of wound healing.

questions.explanation: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) plays a crucial role in the proliferation phase of wound healing, as it stimulates the proliferation of epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells, promoting tissue repair and regeneration.

options.text: Administer antibiotics and leave the wound open

options.text: Debride the wound and apply a dressing
options.explanation: Debriding the wound and applying a dressing is the most appropriate initial management of a wound infection.

options.text: Irrigate the wound with saline and apply a topical antibiotic
options.explanation: Irrigating the wound with saline and applying a topical antibiotic is not the most appropriate initial management of a wound infection.

options.explanation: Closing the wound with sutures and staples is not the most appropriate initial management of a wound infection.

questions.question: A surgeon is evaluating a patient with a chronic wound and notices that the wound is not progressing through the normal stages of wound healing. Which of the following factors can impede the wound healing process?

options.explanation: Diabetes mellitus can impede the wound healing process.
Hypertension is not the primary factor that can impede the wound healing process.
Hyperthyroidism is not the primary factor that can impede the wound healing process.
Asthma is not the primary factor that can impede the wound healing process.

questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus can impede the wound healing process, as it affects the body's ability to regulate blood sugar levels, leading to impaired tissue perfusion, reduced growth factor production, and increased risk of infection.

questions.question: A patient has a wound that requires closure with a suture material that will provide adequate strength for 6-8 weeks. Which of the following suture materials is most suitable for this purpose?

Monocryl (absorbable) is not the most suitable suture material for this purpose.
PDS (absorbable) is the most suitable suture material for this purpose.
Nylon (non-absorbable) is not the most suitable suture material for this purpose.

questions.explanation: PDS (absorbable) is the most suitable suture material for this purpose, as it provides adequate strength for 6-8 weeks, allowing for sufficient tissue healing before being absorbed by the body.
